{{Recipe}}

'''Accra cassava''' is a popular cassava fritter eaten in Cameroon. It can be eaten as breakfast, lunch, or dinner and is best enjoyed fresh.

== Ingredients ==

* 3 [[Cookbook:Pound|pounds]] [[Cookbook:Grating|grated]] [[Cookbook:Cassava|cassava]] (can be frozen and thawed)
* 4 large, overly ripe [[Cookbook:Banana|bananas]] (optional)
* 1 [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|teaspoon]] or more of [[Cookbook:Salt|salt]]
* A good amount of [[Cookbook:Vegetable oil|vegetable oil]]

== Procedure ==

# Squeeze the grated cassava using a kitchen cloth or [[Cookbook:Cheesecloth|cheesecloth]] (like the one used for preparing homemade pap) to remove as much liquid as possible. The cassava should be very dry with little liquid.
# [[Cookbook:Mashing|Mash]] the bananas well using a fork, [[Cookbook:Potato Masher|masher]], or [[Cookbook:Food Processor|food processor]].
# Add the cassava and salt to the mashed banana in a medium sized bowl, and mix them together very well. The mixture should be firm enough that it can be rolled into balls.
# Use your palms to roll about 2 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tablespoons]] of the mixture into bite-size balls.
# Heat the vegetable oil to 375 °F in a deep [[Cookbook:Frying Pan|skillet]] or a [[Cookbook:Saucepan|saucepan]]. You can check the oil temperature by dropping in a 1-[[Cookbook:Inch|inch]] square of bread—it should take about 1 minute to brown.
# Place the cassava balls gently into the hot oil and fry until golden brown. Do not overcrowd the pan—work in batches as necessary.
# Remove the fritters from the hot oil, drain, and serve fresh.
